simple.meaning: אֶדֶר (ʼeder) is a Hebrew object word meaning “amplitude , i.e. (concrete) a mantle ; also (figuratively) splendor.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Micah 2:8. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֶדֶר (H145) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֶדֶר (ʼeder) / H145 is traced through Micah 2:8, Zechariah 11:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: amplitude , i.e. (concrete) a mantle ; also (figuratively) splendor
definitions.full: H145. eder אֶ֫דֶר noun [masculine] 1 glory, magnificence (Assyrian aduru , adiru ) ironical of price of shepherd (symbolic) Zech 11:13 . 2 mangle, cloak (as wide ) Micah 2:8 (|| שַׂלְמָה ), but read אדרת ( ת lost before following ת ), so WRS Proph 427 .

occurrences.englishText: But lately my people have risen up as an enemy.
Yahweh said to me, “Throw it to the potter, the handsome price that I was valued at by them!” I took the thirty pieces of silver, and threw them to the potter, in Yahweh’s house.
